tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Existence of an asymptotic shrinking soliton] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0134, page-0135, page-0136, page-0137 ↗ def:chow-iii-kappa-solution ↗ lem:chow-iii-reduced-distance-two-point ↗ thm:chow-iii-reduced-volume-monotonicity 1. ch19:19.53\group Reduced Geometry

For every sequence $\tau _i\to \infty $ in a $\kappa $-solution there are points $q_i$ with $\ell (q_i,\tau _i)\le n/2$ and a subsequence for which $(M,\tau _i^{-1}g(\tau _i\theta ),q_i)$ converges to a complete nonflat gradient shrinking soliton. The limit satisfies the trace Harnack estimate and is a $\kappa $-solution with Harnack; in dimension three it has bounded $\Rm \ge 0$. The reduced distances converge locally and the mock reduced volume equals the limit of the reduced volumes.
